author: builder for the finops-cost-lead review (advises, does not sign off)
note: Four further reference scenarios (PLAN F5 item 4), labelled illustrative, built from published provider customer stories and case studies (AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud). Expected outcomes were written BEFORE running the engine, by applying DESIGN.md sections 3, 5, 9 and 10 by hand (a throwaway calculation sheet outside the repository, using exact inputs so the arithmetic is checkable). Sources supply shape only and were read through search-result text (status S), because the proxy blocks the provider sites. No outcome figure from a source is used as an input or benchmark. Money is in each scenario's currency; no FX in value. Same schema as reference-scenarios.json; F5-scenario-diffs.md records the comparison with the engine.

conventions.valueFields: levers and totals are annual run-rate gross unless prefixed net; year 1 applies the ASM-FIN-045 ramp from each lever's start month (ASM-FIN-064)

scenarios.name: Global energy company on Azure with an established cost-governance practice (executive mode)
scenarios.summary: Shape from a Microsoft customer story: an energy major whose platform team uses Microsoft Cost Management with Azure Policy for governance, asks engineers to shut idle virtual machines at weekends and delete orphaned storage, and reports lower cloud cost while Azure usage grew. Spend, shares and answers are scenario assumptions.

sources.usedFor: Shape only: Azure-first energy company; cost monitoring with Microsoft Cost Management and Azure Policy over several years; weekend shut-down of idle VMs (OP-06 Walk: some teams) and orphaned-storage clean-up (OP-05 Walk). Read through search-result text only; the provider site is blocked by the proxy, so the page itself was not opened. No outcome figure from the source is used as an input or benchmark. The story's "40 percent" figure is not used.

scenarios.tolerance: Ratings, gaps, severities and finding IDs must match exactly. Money figures within 1% (rounding) or the difference explained in F5-scenario-diffs.md.
reasoning: Tier 2: USD 60M spend (3 points) and 20+ consuming units (+1).
Seven of eight executive capabilities at or above target; only Executive Strategy Alignment (MP-04 Crawl) is below.

LEV-04: 33M compute x 20% non-production x 50% unscheduled (OP-06 Walk -> 0.5, ASM-FIN-052) = 3.30M base x 70.2% = 2.32M upper; expected 1.16M. Its net run-rate is 1.92% of P, just under the 2% uplift, so its lever finding stays Medium.
LEV-01 is zero: steady 60% - coverage 55% - unscheduled non-production 10% < 0. DECISION-02 (High) asks the client not to buy more commitments until scheduling lands.
Need index 14.2: base 4.2 (one one-level gap over 8) + Tier 2 (10); growth 5% adds nothing; expected value 1.9% of P adds nothing. Band "Lightweight practices sufficient at current scale".
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: A long-running cost-governance practice on a large Azure estate should read mostly at target with modest remaining scheduling value and no case for more commitments; the model says the same. The story's own savings figure is not used.

value.label: Indicative value range (conservative / expected / upper), net of estimated implementation cost: not a savings commitment; evidence validation required.

scenarios.tolerance: Ratings, gaps, severities and finding IDs must match exactly. Money figures within 1% (rounding) or the difference explained in F5-scenario-diffs.md.
reasoning: Tier 2: about USD 28.5M (2), Kubernetes material (+1), 5-19 units (+1).
Anomaly Management is Unknown: UN-10 Walk but UN-11 "Don't know", so the core rule gives Unknown, counted as gap 2 (High, unconfirmed). Unknown is risk, not Not yet (D5).
Usage Optimization: OP-04 Crawl lowered one level by OP-05 and OP-06 Not yet -> Not yet, gap 2, High.

LEV-04: (90M compute - 30M clusters) x 25% non-production x 100% unscheduled (OP-06 Not yet -> 0) = 15M x 70.2% = 10.54M upper; expected 5.27M (3.5% of P net, so the uplift is reached but Usage Optimization is already High).
LEV-01: 90M x (70% - 40% - 25%) = 4.5M x 55% = 2.48M upper; expected 1.24M (0.8% of P net): a Medium lever finding, since Rate Optimization is at target.
Both levers start in month 3 (Usage Optimization waits for the Allocation milestone; Rate Optimization is wave 2), so year 1 is 9/12 of the ramp share.
Need index 49.2: base 29.2 (gaps 1+2+1+1+2 = 7 over 8 capabilities) + Tier 2 + growth 25%. Expected value 4.3% of P: no value modifier. Confidence Low (one Unknown).
scenarios.plausibilityCheck: A bank two to three years into a migration with a new FinOps function should show strong practice and commitments but weak usage hygiene and an open data question; the model's scheduling-led value is consistent with that. The story's 30% figure is not used.

reasoning: Tier 1: about USD 6.5M (1) and Kubernetes material (+1); 2-4 units add nothing. Unit Economics and Invoicing & Chargeback have no Tier 1 target and create no finding.
Only Executive Strategy Alignment (MP-04 Not yet) and FinOps Assessment (MP-11 Not yet) are below their Crawl targets: 16 of 18.

LEV-07: 3.0M x (1 - 0.55 / 0.65) = 462k upper, 231k expected (3.8% of P net: High).
